subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the trust boundary that allows generated HTML to remain host-readable after outbound staging?
rationale: The PR intentionally expands a local HTML host-read security boundary beyond the temp root, and that lifecycle is product/security ownership rather than a purely mechanical code fix.

options.title: Accept content-bound provenance after refresh
options.body: Resolve the dirty merge state, then land the PR if final review stays clean and sha256+size SQLite provenance is accepted as the staged generated-HTML trust boundary.

options.title: Require a narrower lifecycle
options.body: Ask for a different ownership, cleanup, or persistence model before merge if persisted outbound trust rows are not acceptable.

options.title: Keep staged HTML fail-closed
options.body: Pause or close this PR and leave generated HTML blocked after staging if maintainers do not want this trust expansion.

recommendation.title: Accept content-bound provenance after refresh
recommendation.body: Resolve the dirty merge state, then land the PR if final review stays clean and sha256+size SQLite provenance is accepted as the staged generated-HTML trust boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the original trusted generated HTML host-read behavior and is the clearest history owner for accepting or changing this boundary.
